stem.text: The price P of a product, in dollars, in a market whose equilibrium price is 60 dollars moves toward the equilibrium price at a rate proportional to the difference between the equilibrium price and P. At time \( t = 0 \) hours, \( P = 80 \). Using k for the positive constant of proportionality, write a differential equation for P as a function of t and state the initial condition.

worked_solution.text: The dependent variable is P and the independent variable is t in hours, so the rate is \( \frac{dP}{dt} \).

Proportional to the difference means a constant multiple of it. With k positive, \( k(60 - P) \) is positive when P is below 60 and negative when it is above, so P moves down toward 60 from its starting value.
The equation is \( \frac{dP}{dt} = k\left(60 - P\right) \), and the initial condition, stated separately, is \( P(0) = 80 \).

options.label: \( \frac{dP}{dt} = k\left(60 - 80\right) \), with \( P(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: the initial value 80 substituted for P inside the equation, so the rate becomes a constant

options.label: \( \frac{dP}{dt} = 60 - P \), with \( P(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: proportional read as equal, so the constant k never appears

options.label: \( \frac{dP}{dt} = k\left(P - 60\right) \), with \( P(0) = 80 \)
options.derivation: the difference written as P minus the level, which with k positive drives P away from 60
